assets.researchSummary: Flare is moving from recovering after a security scare to selling its data network outside Flare. Issuer adoption of the DVN after its December launch is the evidence to watch.
assets.overview: Flare announced on Nov 12 that it will run a LayerZero verifier service (DVN) for cross-chain tokens from early December, starting with Flare and Ethereum: its 100 data providers confirm messages by stake-weighted majority, OFT issuers such as Tether, PayPal, Paxos and Ondo can add it, and each verification is paid in FLR with 90% of fees going to Flare's FIRE reinvestment entity. The same day Spectra's FXRP yield market gained an order book, and Firelight said it now backs vaults on Lido, Kraken and Sentora. This follows the clean Nov 11 activation of the emergency v1.15.1 hard fork after a Nov 10 exploit attempt on upstream node code, with no funds affected. On Nov 14 Flare shared DefiLlama Research's Firelight report, which puts active cover at $51.2 million across five vaults (Firelight is a DefiLlama Research client). On Nov 16 Firelight said higher protocol emissions lift staked-XRP yields to up to 4% APY, funded by cover fees rather than XRPL staking, and the value-locked alert has cleared at −14.8% over 7 days. The main risks are the missing post-mortem and whether issuers actually adopt the DVN.

assets.researchSummary: Integrations keep accumulating, now including Latin American local-currency stablecoin pairs from Ripio, on top of record quarterly figures. The figures are community research, and the Robinhood insider case is a reminder that open venues attract misuse of inside information.
assets.overview: Hyperliquid's growth case rests on a Hyperliquid Research Collective report (Nov 13) putting Q3 open interest at a record $16.8 billion, ahead of Bybit, Kraken and OKX, with revenue up 22% to $191 million and stock-linked HIP-3 perpetuals up 161%. Distribution widened this month: Upbit and Bithumb opened HYPE won markets on Nov 10, Binance added a USDC-margined HYPE perpetual on Nov 11, and Hyperliquid's Nov 16 weekly update listed Bitso integrating Hyperliquid perps through builder codes, Delpho yield products on HyperEVM and Alchemy support for HyperCore data. On Nov 16 a former Robinhood engineer pleaded guilty to wire fraud for trading Hyperliquid perpetuals ahead of Robinhood listings he knew about ($125,523 in profit), a misuse case rather than a Hyperliquid flaw. On Nov 17 Ripio launched wARS and wBRL (Argentine peso and Brazilian real stablecoin) spot pairs against USDC on Hyperliquid and relaunched Ripio Trade as a beta front end to Hyperliquid markets. Elysium's HyperCore hooks upgrade is next, with no fixed date. The main risks are market-structure questions around paid priority-data auctions and speculative flows that may not last.

assets.researchSummary: Two completed infrastructure developments are verified: Coinbase's token conversion and Enso's seven-chain integration. The material data issue is identity: CoinGecko still serves legacy aerodrome-finance separately from successor aero, while DefiLlama's aerodrome fees endpoint resolves to the broader Aero parent.
assets.overview: Aerodrome Finance began as a Base DEX, but the official upgrade hub says Aerodrome and Velodrome became the unified Aero protocol on October 21, 2026. The successor retains the AERO ticker, uses a new Base token contract and replaces legacy weekly voting with sAERO-based continuous reward allocation. Coinbase announced completed AERO/VELO conversion and restored sends and receives on November 6; Aero's November 8 post reiterates that completed exchange migration, rather than announcing another launch. Enso and Aero also confirmed access to the new MetaDEX's swaps, liquidity management and gauge staking across seven chains on November 6. The next evidence to track is successful migration, sustained routed usage and the relationship between actual pool revenue and reward issuance, not a newly verified dated upgrade in the next 60 days. Principal risks are migration and cross-chain contract dependencies, privileged emergency controls, ongoing issuance and mixing legacy Base-only statistics with successor-wide data.

assets.researchSummary: Developers are choosing to protect deployed contracts over Glamsterdam's schedule, with a decision due Nov 19. The MEV acquittal is a notable legal marker for Ethereum's transaction-ordering market.
assets.overview: Ethereum's next upgrade, Glamsterdam, remains on hold with no Hoodi or mainnet date. On the Nov 16 testing call Ethereum Foundation developer Marius van der Wijden estimated that the EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 gas repricing could disrupt up to 15,000 of roughly 90 million deployed contracts, with a few hundred thousand dollars potentially at risk, and independent audits have found hundreds of compatibility problems; core developers reconsider the proposals on Thursday, Nov 19. On Nov 16 a US judge acquitted the Peraire-Bueno brothers in the first criminal case over an Ethereum MEV exploit, finding no material misrepresentation. Earlier this month LlamaRisk proposed narrowing Aave V3's Core market to blue-chip collateral and xStocks launched UK and EU equities with Ethereum among its chains. The main risk is that a revised or delayed Glamsterdam pushes back the scaling gains the roadmap depends on.

assets.overview: VeChain's current ecosystem combines VeChainThor, the VeBetter application network, VeWorld and the AgentSuite agent-development offering. Its published Hayabusa model ties VTHO reward issuance to actively delegated VET, with VTHO used for gas and base fees burned; VET and VTHO therefore need separate treatment. A November 6 VeChain post highlighted Greencart's Kapok shopping agent and a developer-reported 250 Amazon orders in a week, with human approval retained. That figure originated in Greencart's November 4 post, so it is older context amplified in the review window, not a newly audited November 6 adoption milestone. The Interstellar VIP-255 publication proposes newer EVM features while preserving tokenomics, but this review did not independently verify its later activation block or a new dated event in the next 60 days. The key risk is mistaking rewarded consumer actions or agent demonstrations for durable paid demand, alongside validator-delegation concentration and application-security dependencies.

Its current ecosystem also includes XDC AI agent-payment infrastructure. Keyban's partner announcement, dated November 1 in its header and November 2 in its body, describes separate non-custodial agent accounts, USDC-per-call API payments and spending limits set by businesses. marketAlerts.change: CFTC approves Backpack as a US designated contract market and clearing house for blockchain-based derivatives
marketAlerts.summary: Backpack announced on Nov 16 that the CFTC approved its US entity TLD Markets as a Designated Contract Market and TLD Clearing as a Derivatives Clearing Organization. Backpack plans to let US users trade leveraged crypto perpetuals around the clock with fiat or crypto collateral and cross-margining, drawing on its global liquidity through one unified order book. Trading is not live yet and no launch date has been announced. Backpack is a Solana-native exchange and wallet, and its CEO spoke at Breakpoint the same day.
marketAlerts.why: It is a regulatory first: US-approved perpetuals sharing one global order book with offshore users, which could bring onchain-style derivatives to US traders through a regulated venue. It does not change any focus network directly, but it widens the regulated path for crypto derivatives that Hyperliquid and other offshore venues serve today.

marketAlerts.change: US judge acquits the Peraire-Bueno brothers in the first criminal case over an Ethereum MEV exploit
marketAlerts.summary: US District Judge Jessica Clarke in Manhattan granted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno a judgment of acquittal on Nov 16 on wire fraud, wire-fraud conspiracy and money-laundering conspiracy charges over their 2023 scheme, in which they baited Ethereum trading bots and exploited a relay software flaw to take about $25 million in 12 seconds. She ruled that prosecutors had not proved a material misrepresentation, which wire fraud requires, and directed the clerk to close the case. A jury had deadlocked in November 2025, leading to a mistrial. The ruling was widely reported on Nov 17 and 18.
marketAlerts.why: It was the US government's first criminal case over MEV, the profit from ordering transactions on a public chain, and the outcome suggests that outwitting bots through the protocol's own rules is not automatically fraud. That matters for validators, searchers and relay operators on Ethereum and other focus chains, although it does not settle civil liability or every possible charge.

marketAlerts.change: Trezor says a breach at shipping partner Skladon exposed customer details from about 27,000 orders
marketAlerts.summary: Hardware-wallet maker Trezor disclosed on Nov 16 that its shipping partner Skladon notified it on Nov 15 of unauthorized access to systems holding Trezor customer shipping data, from a breach on Nov 7. Trezor believes the attacker exported data for about 27,000 orders placed between Aug 9 and Nov 7, including full names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, email addresses and order details. Trezor says its own systems and devices were not compromised, and it is introducing anonymous pickup in most European countries and cutting order-data retention from 90 to 45 days. It warns affected customers about scam calls, texts and letters and potential physical-security risks.
marketAlerts.why: Names and home addresses of known hardware-wallet buyers are a target list for phishing and physical 'wrench' attacks, and this is Trezor's second vendor-side exposure in recent weeks. Coins held on Trezor devices are not at risk as long as owners never share their recovery phrase.

marketAlerts.change: About $6.4M drained from one Safe multisig through a Zodiac Roles permission; no contract flaw found
marketAlerts.summary: An attacker moved roughly $6.4 million in USDC and syrupUSDC out of a single Safe multisig early on Monday, Nov 16, through Zodiac's Roles Modifier, a third-party add-on that lets designated role members act for the wallet without owner signatures. PeckShield flagged the loss at $6.45 million. Zodiac says it found no flaw in its contracts and that a probably compromised role-member key sent a transaction that a custom policy allowed but likely never intended. Safe says only one multisig was affected, no owner signed, and its contracts and Safe{Wallet} app were not affected.
marketAlerts.why: Safe multisigs hold treasuries for many DAOs and funds, and this shows that add-on permission modules can bypass the multi-owner approval people rely on. No focus network is affected; the lesson is to audit delegated roles on any multisig.

marketAlerts.change: Lighter pauses withdrawals after a leaked trader API key lets an attacker pull about $10.4M in USDC; about $5M returned
marketAlerts.summary: Perpetual-futures exchange Lighter suspended all withdrawals shortly after 11:00 UTC (5 AM CST) on Monday, Nov 16, after an attacker took control of one trader's API keys and withdrew funds; Bitquery traced $10.39 million in USDC leaving Lighter's Ethereum contract and swapped into ETH within minutes, and researchers put potential losses across two market-maker accounts at up to $15.5 million, a figure Lighter has not confirmed. Lighter says the keys were derived from flawed, unofficial signing code used by that trader and that its protocol, smart contracts and infrastructure were not affected. Its Security Council returned about $5 million in USDC to the affected trader, withdrawals resumed about seven hours later, and it is adding IP allowlists and per-key limits. Because the loss came from one user's compromised keys rather than a platform exploit, and part was recovered, it is listed as Medium.
marketAlerts.why: Lighter is one of the larger onchain perpetuals venues competing with Hyperliquid, and the incident shows how third-party trading code can become the weak point even when exchange contracts hold. No focus network was affected, but trading firms running API bots on any perps venue face the same key-handling risk.

marketAlerts.change: Coinone discloses a customer-data breach at its outsourced support contractor; no funds lost
marketAlerts.summary: South Korean exchange Coinone disclosed on Nov 15 that an attacker breached the servers of its outsourced customer-support contractor at around 4 AM KST on Nov 12. Depending on each customer's support history, exposed records may include names, phone numbers, emails, birth dates, bank accounts, passwords, ID numbers, addresses, wallet addresses and transaction IDs. Coinone says its own account, trading and wallet systems were not breached and no funds were lost; customers with no support history are unaffected. It is preparing a lookup service for affected users and warning about follow-on phishing and scam calls.
marketAlerts.why: Coinone is one of South Korea's main won exchanges, and leaked identity, bank and wallet details are exactly what targeted phishing needs. The breach came through a vendor rather than the exchange itself, a recurring weak point. No focus network is affected directly.

news.title: Breakpoint closes: Mitsui commits its gold token to Solana, and Akash, Temporal and the Foundation add 2027 plans
news.body: On Breakpoint's final day in London on Nov 17, Shinsuke Waka, Mitsui & Co.'s Head of Digital Finance, said the Japanese trading house chose Solana for its Zipangcoin (ZPG) gold token, which Mitsui's issuing subsidiary said in April it planned to bring to Solana; no Solana launch date has been announced. Akash Network presented Akash Compute Forwards, a design for a Solana-settled forward market in one-month contracts on eight-GPU Nvidia B300 nodes, with a certified-business pilot targeted for early 2027 subject to audits, legal clearance and default protections. Temporal, the team behind HumidiFi, unveiled Supermassive, a shared-liquidity hub for perpetuals and options across Solana venues, targeting a 2027 launch with a waitlist open. The Solana Foundation also said it is backing CoinGecko's expansion without disclosing terms, and set Breakpoint 2027 for San Francisco on Sept 8–10.
news.why: Mitsui is one of Japan's largest trading houses, so moving a live gold token onto Solana adds a commodity-tokenization reference to this week's bank and market-infrastructure commitments. The derivatives and GPU-market plans are 2027 projects, so the near-term proof point is the ZPG launch itself.

news.title: Glamsterdam gas changes could break up to 15,000 Ethereum contracts; testing stays paused before Thursday's call
news.body: Ethereum Foundation developer Marius van der Wijden told the Nov 16 developer call that the gas repricing in EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, part of the planned Glamsterdam upgrade, could disrupt up to 15,000 deployed contracts out of roughly 90 million, with a few hundred thousand dollars potentially at risk, CoinDesk reported on Nov 17. The changes raise the cost of operations that grow Ethereum's state, which can break apps built around fixed gas allowances or predictable costs. Independent audits have found hundreds of separate compatibility problems, testing on the Hoodi testnet is paused, and Glamsterdam has no confirmed release date. Core developers are due to reconsider the proposals on the All Core Devs call on Thursday, Nov 19.
news.why: Glamsterdam carries Ethereum's next round of base-layer scaling, so a redesign or longer delay pushes back roadmap gains. Developers putting deployed contracts ahead of the schedule lowers the risk of a broken upgrade, and Thursday's call should set the new path.
news.tagReason: A cautious delay to protect deployed contracts; decision due Nov 19.

It also relaunched Ripio Trade as a beta app that gives users a simple interface to Hyperliquid markets in Spanish and Portuguese; orders execute and settle on Hyperliquid, not on Ripio. No volumes for the new pairs have been published yet.
news.why: It adds local-currency on-ramps for two of Latin America's largest crypto markets and routes a regional app's users onto Hyperliquid through a front end, the distribution model behind much of Hyperliquid's recent growth. The test is whether real peso and real liquidity shows up on the new pairs.
news.tagReason: New local-currency pairs and a front end routing Latin American users to Hyperliquid.

news.title: Nvidia reports $115.8 billion Q3 revenue, up 103%, and guides Q4 to $130 billion
news.body: Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion for the quarter ended Oct 25, up 20% from the previous quarter and 103% from a year earlier, with data-center revenue of $107.6 billion, up 110%. GAAP gross margin was 74.8% and GAAP diluted earnings were $2.70 a share. It guided fourth-quarter revenue, which includes an extra week, to $130 billion plus or minus 3%, again assuming no data-center compute revenue from China, and said Vera Rubin NVL72 systems have shipped. It was the first report under interim CEO Colette Kress, who said the roadmap is on track.
news.why: It is the first hard read on demand since Jensen Huang's exit, and it shows the AI build-out that also drives GPU-marketplace networks such as Render, Akash and Bittensor subnets is still growing fast. Succession and China export policy remain the open questions.
news.tagReason: Record quarter and higher guidance under interim leadership.

Musk has said owner-car trials could start next month, which has not been confirmed in a filing.
news.why: Service-area growth in a new metro is the practical measure of Tesla's autonomy push, which is now central to its strategy. Tesla has no current crypto product tie beyond its bitcoin holdings.

news.title: Breakpoint's institutional wave: Zelle picks Solana for ZelleUSD, Bullish, ICE and Allfunds commit, and Solana becomes 1.0
news.body: Over Breakpoint's first two days (Nov 15–16), Zelle, the US bank-owned payments network, said its ZelleUSD stablecoin will launch on Solana for international person-to-person payments; Bullish agreed a $4.2 billion purchase of transfer agent Equiniti, paid partly in tokenized BLSH shares on Solana (close expected January 2027, subject to approvals); ICE Digital Trust began custodying SOL collateral for Abra loans; and Allfunds named 22 asset managers for Project Harmonia tokenized funds from Q1 2027. The Solana Foundation retired the 'mainnet beta' label for Solana 1.0, one protocol version shared by the Agave and Firedancer clients, and asked validators to patch the NoisyTCP Linux kernel flaw. On Nov 15 Solflare launched Private Mode, which hides balances and amounts on Helius's Privacy Rings, and Meteora launched DLX. ZelleUSD has no launch date, and most of the institutional items run into 2027.
news.why: Together with DTCC's Nov 12 plan to connect in 2H 2027, this is the broadest set of institutional commitments any focus network has drawn this year, spanning payments, transfer agency, custody and fund distribution. The gap between announcement and live usage is the main thing to track.
news.tagReason: Broad institutional commitments, mostly with 2027 or conditional delivery.

news.title: NEAR ratifies a cut in maximum issuance from 2.5% to 1.6% and adds stocks and ETFs to near.com
news.body: House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on Nov 16 after the Security Council's 14-day review window closed with no veto. NEAR's maximum annual issuance will step down a small amount every epoch once the reduction begins, reaching 1.6% after 24 months, from 2.5% since the October 2025 halving; NEAR says realized gross issuance was 2.45% in September 2026 because fees are burned. It is NEAR's second inflation cut in just over a year. On Nov 17 NEAR also said near.com now offers tokenized stocks and ETFs alongside its other assets, building on its Ondo integration.
news.why: Lower issuance cuts the dilution NEAR holders and validators absorb, and it is a governance-settled change on a published schedule rather than a proposal. It also lowers staking rewards over time, so validator economics will lean more on fees from products such as NEAR Intents.
news.tagReason: Ratified issuance cut with a verifiable onchain schedule.

news.title: Polkadot approves the second validator cut: the active set drops from 500 to 400 on Nov 18
news.body: Polkadot Referendum 1969, the second step of the validator-set reduction, passed on Subsquare with 99.4% aye (about 34.7 million DOT for and 200,000 against). It executes at relay block 33,929,900, around midday CET (about 5 AM CST) on Wednesday, Nov 18, setting the validator count to 400 and adjusting a budget allocation and a relay-chain approval setting. It follows Referendum 1966, enacted Nov 10, which cut the set to 500, and the Nov 11 strategy vote (Referendum 1954) that refocused Polkadot on users and dotUSD. Nominators backing validators that fall outside the top 400 will stop earning rewards and may need to re-nominate.
news.why: Fewer validators lowers what Polkadot pays for security, in line with its cost-cutting strategy, but concentrates stake among a smaller set. It is a settled governance outcome now, not a proposal, so the practical item is for DOT stakers to check their nominations after Nov 18.
news.tagReason: Passed governance that trims security costs but concentrates stake.

news.body: Nvidia's board is not weighing a return for founder Jensen Huang as chief executive and is focused on the independent investigation into his conduct, CNBC, Politico and the BBC reported on Nov 16. news.title: US Commerce rule requires licenses for advanced AI chips in overseas data centers serving Chinese companies
news.body: On Nov 16 the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule requiring licenses to send advanced AI chips and servers to overseas data centers that provide large amounts of compute (above 12 million aggregate TPP) to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other restricted destinations. It also requires licenses for advanced-chip sales to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, with strict customer due-diligence rules. Existing data-center arrangements have 90 days to obtain a license.
news.why: It closes the remote-access route Chinese firms have used to reach US AI chips through third-country data centers, which adds licensing friction to Nvidia and AMD sales in fast-growing Southeast Asian and Brazilian markets. The commercial effect depends on how licenses are granted.
news.tagReason: New licensing friction on AI-chip sales in several growth markets.

news.title: Google's threat-intelligence group says 'the era of autonomous attacks has arrived'
news.body: Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) published its Q4 AI Threat Tracker on Nov 16, saying attackers now use multi-agent AI frameworks to automate reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, patch analysis, exploit writing and execution. GTIG says it observed a tool it calls exploit_agent turn a security patch into a working exploit with no human in the loop, and CyberScoop reports Google attributed the first fully automated AI cyberattack to Russian-speaking actors. Google expects sophisticated fully autonomous attacks within three to six months.
news.why: It is a high-profile warning that AI is shrinking the time between a patch and an exploit, which matters for every software operator, crypto exchanges and validators included; Luxor described an AI-enabled attack on its mining software the same weekend. It also supports demand for Google Cloud's security products.
news.tagReason: Influential security research; no change to Google's business.

news.body: Shareholders filed a class action against Intel, its CEO and CFO alleging the company concealed how severe a PC-sales slowdown was before a 28.6% one-day share drop, the BBC and Ars Technica reported on Nov 16. weeklyRecap.title: Week in context · Nov 4–10, 2026
weeklyRecap.body:
The week's main theme was distribution moving into regulated and mainstream channels. Solana gained Formation's SEC-exemption notice for a tokenized-securities venue, a Schwab Crypto listing, a native privacy layer from Helius and one-tap trading from X cashtags; NEAR Intents went live in Talos's institutional system; HYPE gained won markets on Upbit and Bithumb plus the Elysium L2; and Ondo brought Fidelity's FCAT into every tokenized-stock bridge transfer. Bittensor's Gamma Tokens went live as a protocol payment rail, though first-day use was tiny.

Governance moved from votes to execution. Polkadot enacted Referendum 1966's 500-validator target on Nov 10, while Acala and Karura proposed shutting down in February 2027. Render's RNP-024 closed with only yes votes shown but no official announcement, and the XRPL Foundation's quantum-safe account design remains a draft with a 2027 study.

Security is the cross-watchlist caution. Flare forced an emergency hard fork after an exploit attempt, NEAR AI contained a cloud intrusion, and Elliptic traced Binance-hack laundering through NEAR memecoins. Market-wide incidents at Keplr/Web3Auth, LNbits, Ankr, Arcus, Initia and Across were each below the High threshold. Nothing in this recap is a price forecast or financial advice.

stocks.name: Tesla, Inc.
stocks.overview: Tesla builds electric vehicles and energy-storage systems and is investing heavily in self-driving (FSD, Robotaxi and the Cybercab), Optimus robots and its own AI compute. In Q3 2026 revenue was $28.05 billion, roughly flat year over year, with 486,532 deliveries (down about 2%) and net income attributable to common stockholders of $787 million ($0.22 per diluted share), down from $1.37 billion a year earlier; energy revenue fell 16% while services and other rose 33%. Recent moves include Cybercab service starting in Austin in September, a new €100 million Berlin engineering center that opened Nov 4 with about 250 staff, and an official Argentina launch set for Nov 20. Shareholders meet on Dec 3, and Tesla and SpaceX have discussed a possible combination, though no terms have been announced and any deal would need shareholder approval. The main near-term risk is political: after Democrats won Congress and Texas, Tesla and SpaceX shares fell about 11% and 9% on Nov 5, as investors priced in possible congressional probes and tighter rules on AI data centers.
stocks.researchSummary: Tesla's latest quarter showed flat revenue and lower profit, with a pivot in spending toward AI compute, robotaxis and robots. This week's company news was constructive (the Berlin engineering hub and the Argentina entry), but after the midterms the bigger story is the regulatory and political overhang on Elon Musk's companies.
stocks.cryptoLink: Tesla's Q3 2026 10-Q shows digital assets of $962 million at Sep 30, 2026, mostly 11,509 bitcoin acquired for $386 million, and the company booked a $288 million mark-to-market gain on its bitcoin in the quarter.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
stocks.overview: Meta runs Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, earns almost all of its revenue from advertising, and is spending heavily to build its Muse AI assistant and 'personal superintelligence'. Q3 2026 revenue rose 26% to $64.60 billion and diluted EPS was $3.83, or $7.40 excluding a $9.89 billion charge from its settlement with state attorneys general over teen mental health. Capital expenditures were $34.91 billion in the quarter and free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion. Meta expects 2026 capex of $135–145 billion and Q4 revenue of $73–76 billion. To fund the AI build-out it sold $15 billion of US-dollar bonds on Nov 3 and its first euro bonds (€9 billion) on Nov 4, and it has announced a non-voting Class C share class effective Jan 19, 2027. It launched Muse 'spaces' on Nov 6. The main risks are funding and returns on AI spending: S&P moved Meta's outlook to negative, and more youth-related trials are scheduled.
stocks.researchSummary: Meta's ad business is growing fast, but AI infrastructure spending has pushed free cash flow negative, so it is now raising large amounts of debt and planning equity. Product momentum in Muse continues, while litigation and data-center permitting after the midterms are the main watch items.
stocks.cryptoLink: Since April 2026, Meta has paid select creators in Colombia and the Philippines in Circle's USDC on Solana or Polygon via Stripe. It is not issuing its own stablecoin.

flags.text: Q3 included a $9.89 billion charge from a settlement with 52 state attorneys general of up to about $18.59 billion, and Meta says more youth-related trials are scheduled in the U.S. in the coming months.

Meta's capex of $135–145 billion turned Q3 free cash flow negative, S&P revised its outlook to AA- negative, and Meta's president said after the midterms that building data centers is 'going to be harder'.
Advertising was $63.06 billion of $64.60 billion in Q3 revenue. The new Class C structure is designed to keep Mark Zuckerberg in control, under a Founder Alignment Agreement.

stocks.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
stocks.overview: Alphabet owns Google Search, YouTube, Android, Google Cloud and the Gemini AI models, and sells its TPU AI chips through Google Cloud. Q3 2026 revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion, Google Cloud revenue more than doubled (+103%) to $30.7 billion with $11.1 billion of operating income, and EPS was $2.12; the Gemini app has reached one billion users. This week Google announced a $15 billion data-center investment in Malaysia for 2027–2028 (Nov 4) and a $17 billion first data center in Laramie County, Wyoming (Nov 5), powered partly by a 702 MW Bloom fuel-cell system with carbon capture. Alphabet pays a $0.22 quarterly dividend on Dec 14 to holders of record on Dec 7. The main risk is legal: appeals are pending in both U.S. antitrust cases (search and ad tech), and a court refused to pause related private ad-tech suits.
stocks.researchSummary: Google Cloud is now Alphabet's fastest-growing engine, driven by AI infrastructure and TPU demand, and Google is committing tens of billions more to data centers even as U.S. local opposition grows. Antitrust remedies remain the key overhang.
stocks.cryptoLink: Google Cloud offers Universal Ledger, a managed, permissioned distributed ledger for tokenizing commercial bank money and securities and for wholesale payments.

stocks.name: NVIDIA Corporation
stocks.overview: Nvidia designs the GPUs, CPUs, networking and software that run most AI training and inference. On Nov 12 it announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as president, CEO and director, effective Nov 11; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while remaining CFO, Harvey C. Jones became the board's first chair, and the board is searching internal and external candidates. In Q2 fiscal 2027 (to July 26, 2026) revenue rose 106% to $96.2 billion with data center revenue of $89.0 billion, and Nvidia guided Q3 revenue to $108.0 billion ±2%, assuming no data-center compute revenue from China. On Nov 17 it reported Q3 fiscal 2027 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103%, with data-center revenue of $107.6 billion, guided Q4 to $130 billion ±3% (including an extra week and again no China data-center compute), and said Vera Rubin NVL72 systems have shipped. The main risks are leadership succession, the national-security questions around Huang's departure, and export-policy scrutiny of China chip sales.
stocks.researchSummary: The first report since Jensen Huang's exit showed record revenue and higher guidance, easing the near-term demand question. Succession and China export policy remain the key checkpoints.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
stocks.overview: AMD makes EPYC server CPUs, Instinct AI GPUs, Ryzen PC chips and embedded and gaming silicon. Q3 2026 revenue was a record $13.4 billion (+45%), data center revenue nearly doubled (+97%) to $8.5 billion on the MI450 launch and EPYC demand, and diluted EPS was $1.46 GAAP and $2.09 non-GAAP. Gaming revenue fell 40% to $773 million. AMD guided Q4 revenue to about $17 billion ±3% as it scales Helios rack systems and 'Venice' CPUs, and it filed its 10-Q on Nov 4. It is scheduled to present at the UBS conference on Dec 1 and Barclays on Dec 9. The main risk is AI-spending sentiment and supply: AMD shares fell double digits on Nov 5 in the post-midterm chip selloff, and the memory shortage is raising component costs.
stocks.researchSummary: AMD's latest quarter was its strongest on record and it is now mainly a data-center company, with guidance for faster growth in Q4. The stock's sharp drop on Nov 5 reflected sector-wide fears about the AI build-out rather than company-specific news.

stocks.name: Intel Corporation
stocks.overview: Intel designs and manufactures PC and server CPUs and is building a contract foundry business (Intel 14A). Q3 2026 revenue rose 21% to $16.5 billion, Data Center and AI revenue rose 78% to $7.3 billion (its strongest growth in 15 years) and Intel Foundry revenue rose 58%, with GAAP EPS of $0.60 and non-GAAP EPS of $0.52. Q4 guidance is $15.0–16.0 billion of revenue, with an expected PC slowdown through at least the first half of 2027. Recent deals include a multiyear Xeon collaboration with Oracle Cloud, a planned acquisition of Classiq (quantum software) and a $23 billion equity offering. CEO Lip-Bu Tan bought 150,000 shares on Nov 2 at about $64.73 (Form 4 filed Nov 4). The main risks are supply and execution: an accident at the Kiryat Gat fab in Israel will cost about $300 million of Q4 revenue, with a similar hit expected in Q1.
stocks.researchSummary: Intel's data-center demand is outrunning its supply, but a weaker PC outlook and the Israel fab accident produced soft guidance. The CEO's open-market purchase is a notable insider signal, though it is not a forecast.

flags.text: Intel lists the U.S. government's acquisition of significant equity interests in the company, along with export controls and trade policy, among its key risk factors.

Intel says demand for its data-center products 'continues to meaningfully exceed available supply', limited by Intel 3 yields, substrate shortages and the Fab 28 accident, which will cut about $300 million from Q4 revenue and 200 basis points from gross margin.

The turnaround rests on CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who has bought shares personally (150,000 on Nov 2). Client computing is still about half of Intel Products revenue ($8.1 billion of $15.4 billion), which leaves Intel exposed to the PC slowdown.

stocks.name: Amazon.com, Inc. (AWS)
stocks.overview: Amazon is the parent of AWS, the largest cloud provider, alongside its retail, Prime, advertising, devices and newer businesses (Zoox, Amazon Leo satellites, Pharmacy). In Q3 2026 AWS revenue rose 39% to $46.0 billion, its fastest growth in nearly five years and a $184 billion annualized run rate, with $17.8 billion of operating income (38.7% margin). Total net sales rose 12% to $201.9 billion, operating income was a record $28.1 billion and EPS was $1.89. AWS signed new agreements with Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Oracle and others, Bedrock token volume grew nearly 17x and Trainium became easier to adopt through TorchNeuron; CEO Andy Jassy projects AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028. On Nov 5 Amazon launched $0 Uber Eats delivery for Prime members, and AWS re:Invent runs Nov 30–Dec 4 in Las Vegas. The main risk is capital intensity: 2026 cash capex of about $220 billion has pushed trailing free cash flow to an outflow of $42.4 billion.
stocks.researchSummary: AWS is accelerating on AI demand and is the main driver of Amazon's profits, while retail margins hit a record. The trade-off is very heavy AI capex funded partly with new debt, plus rising data-center permitting risk in the U.S.
stocks.cryptoLink: AWS stopped accepting new customers for Amazon Managed Blockchain (Ethereum, Bitcoin, Polygon node access) on Oct 29, 2026, and will end the service on Sep 29, 2027, pointing users to self-managed Node Runners on AWS or partners such as Alchemy and QuickNode.
